title: 一封礼貌但有力的投诉信
title_en: A Polite but Firm Complaint to a Hotel
summary_zh: 订的是安静的海景房，住进的却是对着停车场、每天七点就开工的房间。Nadia 的投诉邮件不吵不闹：先讲事实，再肯定优点，最后提出具体诉求——正式投诉可以照这个结构写。
body: Dear Guest Services Team, I am writing about my recent three-night stay at your hotel, which I booked specifically because your website promised a quiet room with a sea view. Unfortunately, the room I was given faced a busy car park, and building work next door started at seven every morning. When I raised the issue at the front desk on the first day, the staff member was polite but told me that no other rooms were available. Having checked the booking site that evening, however, I could see several sea-view rooms still being offered for the same dates. I want to stress that your staff were friendly throughout, and the breakfast was excellent. My concern is not with any individual, but with how the problem was handled. Had I been told about the building work in advance, I would have chosen different dates or another hotel altogether. As it was, I spent most of my short break tired and frustrated. I would be grateful if you could look into why I was not offered a different room, and let me know what you are able to offer by way of compensation, whether a partial refund or a discount on a future stay. I have attached a copy of my booking confirmation and two photos taken from the room's window. I look forward to hearing from you, and I hope this feedback will help other guests avoid a similar experience. Yours faithfully, Nadia Rahimi

options: The front desk staff were rude to her
The hotel did not deal properly with her room problem
The breakfast was not what the website promised
The hotel charged her for nights she did not stay
questions.evidence: My concern is not with any individual, but with how the problem was handled.

questions.prompt: Why does Nadia doubt that no other rooms were available?
options: Another guest told her about an empty room
She saw sea-view rooms still being offered online
The staff member later admitted it to her
Her confirmation showed a sea-view room number
questions.evidence: I could see several sea-view rooms still being offered for the same dates

vocabulary.example: I chose this flight specifically because it arrives in the morning.
The guide was patient and cheerful throughout the tour.
I felt frustrated when the train was cancelled for the second time.
The company offered free meals as compensation for the long wait.
We got a partial refund because the pool was closed all week.

expressions.note: raise an issue / a concern 是正式场合“提出问题”的说法，比 complain 更中性、更克制。
投诉时先肯定对方做得好的地方，再转回问题，会显得公允、可信。
常与 tell / book / pay 连用：Please let us know in advance.
接在一个假设之后，把话题拉回真实发生的事，对比感很强。

expressions.text: I would be grateful if you could
expressions.note: 正式邮件里最常用的请求句式，客气但不卑微，后接动词原形。
by way of 表示“作为……的方式”，书面语，也可说 by way of apology（作为道歉）。

knowledge.quote: Had I been told about the building work in advance, I would have chosen different dates or another hotel altogether.
knowledge.explanation: 省略 if 的倒装：Had I been told = If I had been told，与过去事实相反，主句用 would have + 过去分词。书面投诉里用它显得克制而正式。

knowledge.quote: Having checked the booking site that evening
knowledge.explanation: having + 过去分词表示“先做完了某事”，再引出主句的发现。分词的逻辑主语必须和主句主语一致，这里都是 I。

knowledge.quote: I would be grateful if you could look into why I was not offered a different room
knowledge.explanation: 主句 would、从句 could 都是情态动词的过去形式，并不表示过去，而是让请求更委婉。正式请求可以直接套用。

speaking: 用 1 分钟口头向前台投诉一个住宿问题（噪音、房型不符等），语气礼貌但坚定，用上 I want to stress that 和 I would be grateful if you could。
writing: 用 120–150 词写一封礼貌的投诉邮件（酒店、餐厅、快递都可）：讲清事实、肯定对方做得好的地方、提出具体诉求，用上 in advance 和 Had I ..., I would have ...。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 Had I been told ..., I would have ... 写一句对某次糟糕服务的礼貌抱怨。
task.model: Had I been told about the building work in advance, I would have chosen different dates or another hotel altogether.

title: 时差到底在“差”什么
title_en: Jet Lag: When Your Body Clock Lands Later Than You Do
summary_zh: 时差不只是坐久了累，而是体内的“生物钟”和当地的太阳对不上了。读完你会明白光线为什么这么关键，以及为什么很多人觉得往东飞更难受。
body: Anyone who has flown across several time zones knows the strange feeling of being wide awake at midnight and desperate for sleep at lunchtime. Jet lag is not simply tiredness from a long journey. It happens because your body runs on an internal clock, a rhythm of roughly a day that tells you when to feel alert, when to get hungry and when to wind down. This clock is set mainly by light. Morning light reaching your eyes signals that the day has begun, while darkness in the evening tells the brain to prepare for sleep. When you land in a new time zone, the local sun is suddenly out of step with your internal schedule. Your watch says it is breakfast time, but your body, still following the old pattern, insists it is the middle of the night. The clock can adjust, but only gradually, shifting a little each day rather than all at once. That is why the first few days of a trip can feel foggy, even if you slept well on the plane. Many people find that flying east is harder than flying west. Travelling west stretches your day, which the body tends to accept fairly easily, whereas travelling east asks it to fall asleep before it feels ready. Not every part of the body adjusts at the same speed, either, so for a while your appetite and your sleepiness may seem to be running on two different schedules. This is why getting outside in daylight and eating at local mealtimes are the habits many travellers rely on to help the clock catch up.

questions.prompt: What is the main cause of jet lag, according to the passage?
options: Sitting still for many hours on a plane
Not sleeping enough during the flight
A body clock that no longer matches local time
Eating meals at unusual times on board
questions.evidence: the local sun is suddenly out of step with your internal schedule

questions.prompt: Why do many people find flying east harder than flying west?
options: Eastward flights are usually much longer
The body must fall asleep before it feels ready
There is less daylight when you arrive in the east
The body finds it hard to accept a longer day
questions.evidence: travelling east asks it to fall asleep before it feels ready

vocabulary.example: The phone has a small internal battery that cannot be removed.
A short walk after lunch helps me stay alert in the afternoon.
The small town gradually grew into a busy city.
My head felt foggy after the long meeting.
The hot weather took away my appetite.

expressions.note: wide 加强语气，常用于本该睡觉却睡不着的时候：At midnight I was still wide awake.
desperate for + 名词表示“极度需要”：desperate for a coffee / desperate for some fresh air。
指一天结束前让身心慢慢松弛：I read a little to wind down before bed.
原指走路步子不齐，引申为节奏、想法跟不上：His ideas are out of step with the times.
与 gradually 相对：Don't try to change everything all at once.
后面常接 with：I need to catch up with my emails after the holiday.

knowledge.quote: Morning light reaching your eyes signals that the day has begun
knowledge.explanation: 主语中心词是 light，reaching your eyes 只是修饰它，所以谓语用单数 signals，不要被离动词更近的 eyes 带成复数。

knowledge.quote: your body, still following the old pattern, insists it is the middle of the night
knowledge.explanation: 现在分词短语插在主语和谓语之间，补充说明身体此刻的状态（主动地“还在按旧规律走”），比再写一个从句更紧凑。

knowledge.quote: whereas travelling east asks it to fall asleep before it feels ready
knowledge.explanation: whereas 引导对比状语从句，把往西飞和往东飞两种情况并排对照；从句里又套了一个 before 时间状语从句。

speaking: 用 1 分钟向朋友解释：为什么倒时差会让人半夜清醒、白天犯困，用上 out of step with 和 all at once。
writing: 用 100–130 词写一段你或你认识的人作息被打乱（倒时差、熬夜等）的经历，并解释原因，用上 not simply 和 whereas。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 X is not simply Y 纠正一个常见的理解（比如“拖延不只是懒”）。
task.model: Jet lag is not simply tiredness from a long journey.

title: 和“计划控”朋友一起旅行
title_en: Travelling with a Friend Who Plans Everything
summary_zh: Leila 的旅行日程精确到喝咖啡的时间，直到某天美术馆突然闭馆、计划全盘落空。这个小故事讲计划与随性之间的平衡，也藏着几个地道的虚拟语气用法。
body: Leila and I have been friends since primary school, so I knew what I was signing up for when we booked a week in the city together. Within a day, she had sent me a colour-coded schedule: breakfast at eight, the castle at nine, a walking tour at eleven, and lunch at a place she had found on a food blog. Even the coffee breaks had their own row. If I hadn't grown up with her, I would probably find it exhausting, but I've learned that planning is how Leila relaxes. She loves looking forward to things, and a full schedule makes her feel safe in a place she doesn't know. Still, by the third day I was secretly wishing we had a single empty afternoon. Then, on Thursday, the plan fell apart. The gallery we were heading to was closed for repairs, and there was nothing about it online. Leila stood on the steps, scrolling through her phone and looking genuinely lost. I suggested we just walk and see where we ended up. She hated the idea for about ten minutes. After that, we found a tiny square where an old man was selling lemons from a cart, wandered down a street of second-hand bookshops, and ate the best soup of the whole trip in a place with no sign outside. That evening, Leila admitted it had been her favourite afternoon. I didn't say anything, but I noticed that her schedule for the next day had a new row in it, labelled simply: wander.

questions.prompt: What is the story mainly about?
options: Why careful planning always saves time on a trip
A planner discovering the pleasure of unplanned time
Two friends who argue and stop travelling together
How the narrator taught Leila to read a map
questions.evidence: Leila admitted it had been her favourite afternoon

questions.prompt: Why did the plan fall apart on Thursday?
options: Leila's phone stopped working
The gallery was unexpectedly closed
It started raining heavily
They got lost on the way to lunch
questions.evidence: The gallery we were heading to was closed for repairs

vocabulary.example: Moving house is exhausting, even with friends to help.
She was genuinely surprised when everyone shouted happy birthday.
He finally admitted that he had forgotten the tickets.
Each box was labelled with the name of a room.

expressions.text: what I was signing up for
expressions.meaning: 自己答应的是什么；心里早有数
expressions.note: sign up for 原意是报名，引申为“既然答应了，就得接受它的全部后果”：You knew what you were signing up for.

expressions.meaning: 用颜色分类标注的日程表
expressions.note: colour-coded 形容用不同颜色区分类别，带一点调侃“计划控”的意味。

expressions.meaning: 计划泡汤了；计划全乱了
expressions.note: fall apart 原意是散架，也用于计划、关系等“崩了”。
景点、道路告示常用说法，类似的还有 closed for the season。
表示不预设目的地、随性出发，口语里很常见：Let's just drive and see where we end up.
look forward to 中的 to 是介词，后面接名词或动名词：I'm looking forward to seeing you.

knowledge.quote: If I hadn't grown up with her, I would probably find it exhausting
knowledge.explanation: 错综条件：if 从句用过去完成时说过去（假如没一起长大），主句用 would + 动词原形说现在的结果（现在会觉得累）。两部分时间不同，时态也不同。

knowledge.quote: I was secretly wishing we had a single empty afternoon
knowledge.explanation: wish 后接一般过去时 had，表示与当时事实相反的愿望——其实日程里一个空闲的下午都没有。

knowledge.quote: Leila stood on the steps, scrolling through her phone and looking genuinely lost.
knowledge.explanation: 两个现在分词短语作伴随状语，描写她站着时同时在做什么、看上去怎样，比用 and 连成三个分句更紧凑。

speaking: 用 1 分钟说说你旅行时是“计划派”还是“随性派”，举一个例子，用上 the plan fell apart 或 see where we ended up。
writing: 用 120–150 词写一次和朋友或家人一起旅行时的小冲突，以及最后怎么化解的，用上 If I hadn't ..., I would ... 和一个 wish 句。

task.prompt: 仿照这句错综条件句（过去没发生 → 现在的结果），写一句关于你自己某个习惯或某段关系的话。
task.model: If I hadn't grown up with her, I would probably find it exhausting

title: 迷路，才是旅行最好的部分
summary_zh: 导航让我们几乎不会迷路，作者却认为“导航失灵”的时刻往往最精彩：被迫抬头看路、和陌生人搭话、撞见指南里没有的街区。观点鲜明，也讲清了什么时候不该冒险。
body: These days, it takes real effort to get lost. A blue dot follows us everywhere, and a calm voice tells us exactly when to turn. I understand why we love it, but I've come to believe that the moments when that dot fails us are often the best part of a trip. Getting lost forces you to pay attention. Instead of staring at a screen, you start reading street names, noticing which way the hill slopes and watching where local people are going. You ask a shopkeeper for help and end up chatting about her grandson. You wander into a neighbourhood that no guidebook mentions, where washing hangs between balconies and children play football against a garage door. On my first visit to a port city years ago, I took a wrong turn looking for a famous fish market. If I hadn't missed that turning, I would never have found the little bakery where I ate breakfast every day for the rest of the week. I'm not arguing that we should throw our phones into the sea. Unless you are short of time, travelling at night or somewhere that feels unsafe, there is no reason to keep the map open every minute. Try putting it away for an hour in the afternoon and following whatever looks interesting. The worst that can happen is that you walk a little further than planned. The best is that you come home with a story nobody else has. After all, the sights everyone photographs will still be there tomorrow, but the street you stumbled onto by accident belongs only to you.

questions.prompt: What is the writer's main opinion?
options: Travellers should stop using phone maps completely
Getting lost now and then can make a trip richer
Guidebooks are more useful than phone maps
Famous sights are no longer worth visiting
questions.evidence: the moments when that dot fails us are often the best part of a trip

questions.prompt: In which situation does the writer think you should keep the map open?
options: When you are in a famous neighbourhood
When you feel tired after a long walk
When you are short of time or feel unsafe
When local people cannot help you
questions.evidence: Unless you are short of time, travelling at night or somewhere that feels unsafe

vocabulary.example: Living abroad forces you to solve problems on your own.
The garden slopes gently down to the river.
We like to wander around the old town after dinner.
We stumbled onto a tiny museum while we were looking for lunch.

expressions.note: it takes + 名词（effort / time / courage）+ to do sth，是很常用的结构。
come to + believe / realise 表示观点是慢慢形成的，比 I think 更有分量。
end up doing 表示原本没打算、最后却做了：We ended up staying for dinner.
字面用于问路，也可以比喻人生中做错选择。
be short of + 名词：short of money / short of staff。

expressions.text: The worst that can happen is that
expressions.note: 劝别人尝试时用来降低风险感，语气轻松。

knowledge.quote: Getting lost forces you to pay attention.
knowledge.explanation: 动名词短语 Getting lost 作主语，谓语用单数 forces。把一种行为当作话题来讨论时，用动名词开头最自然。

knowledge.quote: If I hadn't missed that turning, I would never have found the little bakery
knowledge.explanation: 与过去事实相反的虚拟：if + 过去完成时，主句 would have + 过去分词。讲“幸好当时……”的经历时的经典结构。

knowledge.quote: Unless you are short of time, travelling at night or somewhere that feels unsafe, there is no reason to keep the map open every minute.
knowledge.explanation: unless 后接三个并列的情况，意为“除非……，否则……”。用它给自己的观点加上合理限制，论证显得不偏激。

speaking: 用 1 分钟说说你是否同意“迷路是旅行最好的部分”，举一个自己的例子，用上 I've come to believe that 和 unless。
writing: 用 150–180 词写一篇短评：旅行时该不该一直开着导航？给出至少两个理由和一个让步，用上 The worst that can happen is that。

task.prompt: 仿照这句，用 If I hadn't ..., I would never have ... 写一次“因祸得福”的经历。
task.model: If I hadn't missed that turning, I would never have found the little bakery where I ate breakfast every day for the rest of the week.
